liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jack Straw** (1 review): The three-song opener was a tight, serious groove, packing energy into the shorter benefit format [10]
- **Amazing Grace** (1 review): The reviewer noted this tune was not as good as the first encore, which featured tasty guitar [19]
- **Land Of A Thousand Dances** (1 review): The reviewer found the song lacked musical merit, considering it only historically significant [15]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-01-13.158146.gems.flac1648** (recommended): source not stated; 14 songs; 102 min [1]
- **gd1980-01-13.170738.fm.master.reel.menke.miller.flac24**: FM broadcast; 13 songs; 115 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [3]
- **gd1980-01-13.170773.fm.master.reel.menke.miller.flac1648**: FM broadcast; 13 songs; 115 min [4]
- **gd1980-01-13.sbd.miller.106517.flac16**: soundboard; 13 songs; 103 min; rated 4.25/5 by 12 [5]. Said about its sound: The soundboard recording has a high average quality, though the reviewer wishes more jam space; The ensemble mastery is crystal clear, with the jam section sounding very much like 1980 [12][19]

## Around the show

- Brian Wilson sat at piano while Mike Love teased him cruelly during the Beach Boys set [9]
- The band played a single set for a charity event, combining elements of a full-length show [14]
- Joan Baez, Mickey Thomas, and the Beach Boys provided vocals on the finale tracks [1]
- Carlos Santana and John Cipollina played guitar on Not Fade Away and Sugar Magnolia [1]
- The concert was a Cambodian Refugee Benefit, featuring guests like Santana, Baez, and the Beach Boys [5]
- 1980 had the most concert dates since 1972, marking a high point for the band [16]
- The short show was satisfying, proving the band could have played much shorter concerts [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-01-13.158146.gems.flac1648**: taped by Augustus Owsley Stanley III; transferred by Transferred (Nov 2021) and mastered by Jim Blackwood Speed/pitch adjusted by Jason Chastain Minor repairs, track, FLAC, and pack by Steve Gravel; source: Maxell MX90 cassette from Bear via Jamie Waddell [1]. Also: The source is an upsampled FM broadcast from KSAN San Francisco, originally aired on Dead Legs [1]
- **gd1980-01-13.170738.fm.master.reel.menke.miller.flac24**: taped by Bob Menke; transferred by Recorded and Transferred by Bob Menke Mastered by Charlie Miller  March 30, 2025; source: FM (KMEL-FM) > Reel Master (Technics 1506 1/4 track 10inch 7.5ips) [3]. Also: The recording is a master reel-to-reel tape, converted from 24-bit/96kHz to 16-bit/48kHz [3]
- **gd1980-01-13.170773.fm.master.reel.menke.miller.flac1648**: taped by Bob Menke; transferred by ecorded and Transferred by Bob Menke Mastered by Charlie Miller  March 30, 2025; source: FM (KMEL-FM) > Reel Master (Technics 1506 1/4 track 10inch 7.5ips) [4]. Also: The file was converted and downsampled using Foobar2000 and dBPoweramp by the uploader [4]
- **gd1980-01-13.sbd.miller.106517.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Dat [5]. Also: The reviewer possessed a degraded cassette copy from the early 1980s before finding this digital file [13]
